answer: The protocol enforces sybil resistance by requiring agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards, verified through unpredictable retrieval audits where any failed proof of replication triggers a non-refundable slash. Like shale layers resisting erosion, each shard anchors identity. A willow branch bends to verify the stream, while karst topography hides deep storage nodes. An honest agent incurs a baseline cost, while 1,000 fakes pay 1,000 times that expense.
